knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonsmooth ℓ1 Exact-Penalty Principle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the ℓ1 residual penalty and records its threshold-based local-minimizer transfers, convex equivalence, and nonconvex failure boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le 0\), \(i=1,\ldots,p\), and \(h_j(x)=0\), \(j=1,\ldots,q\), where all problem functions are locally Lipschitz. For \(r>0\), define
\[
F_r(x)=f(x)+r\left(\sum_{i=1}^p\max\{0,g_i(x)\}+\sum_{j=1}^q|h_j(x)|\right).
\]
This penalty is generally nonsmooth even when the problem functions are smooth. Under the source's stated mild exactness assumptions, there is a finite \(r_l>0\) such that every constrained local minimizer locally minimizes \(F_r\) for every \(r>r_l\). Conversely, a feasible local minimizer of \(F_r\) is a constrained local minimizer if all equality-constraint functions \(h_j\) are smooth. When the constrained problem and \(F_r\) are convex, their minimizer sets coincide for sufficiently large \(r\). Without convexity, an infeasible point may remain a local minimizer of \(F_r\) for every sufficiently large \(r\), even though the constrained problem has feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ℓ1 penalty adds positive inequality violations and absolute equality residuals to the objective and is generally nonsmooth. Under the source's unspecified mild exactness assumptions, constrained local minimizers transfer to the penalty problem above a finite threshold. A feasible penalty local minimizer transfers back when the equality constraints are smooth. Convexity yields identical minimizer sets for sufficiently large penalties, while nonconvex problems can retain infeasible local penalty minimizers.
assumptions_latex: f,g_i,h_j:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\text{ are locally Lipschitz}
\text{The forward transfer requires the source's unspecified mild exactness assumptions}
x^*\in\operatorname{Feas}(P)\text{ and every }h_j\text{ is smooth for the reverse transfer}
P\text{ and }F_r\text{ are convex for equality of their minimizer sets}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists r_l>0\ \forall r>r_l:\operatorname{LocMin}(P)\subseteq\operatorname{LocMin}(F_r);\qquad x^*\in\operatorname{LocMin}(F_r)\cap\operatorname{Feas}(P)\Rightarrow x^*\in\operatorname{LocMin}(P).\text{ Under convexity the minimizer sets coincide, whereas nonconvexity permits persistent infeasible local minimizers of }F_r.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Penalty Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global exactness of an unconstrained penalty reformulation for a Lipschitz constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,\varphi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be Lipschitz, suppose \(\varphi(x)\ge 0\) for every \(x\), and let \(\varnothing\ne\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\varphi(x)=0\}\). For \(A\ge0\), define \(F_A(x)=f(x)+A\varphi(x)\). The function \(F_A\) is a penalty function, and it is an exact penalty function if \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}F_A(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\Omega}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The penalized objective is an exact penalty function when its global minimizers coincide exactly with the global minimizers of the original objective over the feasible zero set of the nonnegative violation function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_A\text{ is exact}\iff \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}F_A(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\Omega}f(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Distance Function and Associated Nonsmooth Exact Penalty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Terminological definition from the source; it does not independently establish a finite exactness threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convex function h:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R} with h(0)=0 is called a strong distance function if there exists \delta>0 such that h(c)\geq\delta\lVert c\rVert_1 for every c\in\mathbb{R}^m. For such h, \sigma>0, and the constraint-violation map c^{(-)}, the associated nonsmooth exact penalty function is P_{\sigma,h}(x)=f(x)+\sigma h(c^{(-)}(x)).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strong distance function is a convex function vanishing at zero that uniformly dominates a positive multiple of the l1 norm. The source calls the resulting violation-penalized objective a nonsmooth exact penalty function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_{\sigma,h}(x):=f(x)+\sigma h(c^{(-)}(x))\text{ is termed the associated nonsmooth exact penalty function.}

knowledge_statements.title: Error-Bound-Based Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local exactness from objective Lipschitz continuity and a constraint error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be a metric space, let \(F\subset X\) be closed, and let \(x^*\in F\) locally minimize \(f\) over \(F\). Suppose on a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x^*\), the function \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz and a violation measure \(V\geq0\) satisfies \(V^{-1}(0)=F\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\leq\kappa V(x)\). Then every \(\rho>L\kappa\) makes \(x^*\) a local minimizer of \(P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho V(x)\). Thus the error-bound modulus and objective Lipschitz modulus give the exactness threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local error bound converts violation into distance, making a linear penalty exact whenever its parameter exceeds the Lipschitz constant times the error-bound modulus.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\) locally minimizes \(f\) over the closed set \(F\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\rho>L\kappa\), \(x^*\) locally minimizes \(P_\rho=f+\rho V\).

notation.meaning: local Lipschitz modulus of the objective

knowledge_statements.title: Calmness-Based Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global linear-penalty exactness derived from calmness below of the perturbation value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_\rho(x):=f(x)+\rho g(x)\). If \(v(t)\ge v(0)-Lt\) for all \(t\ge0\), then every \(\rho>L\) satisfies \[\inf_{x\in X}P_\rho(x)=v(0).\] Moreover, every minimizer of \(P_\rho\) is feasible and minimizes \(f\) over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the perturbation value can decrease by at most L per unit violation, every penalty weight larger than L preserves the constrained value and makes all attained penalized minimizers constrained-optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(v(t):=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\le t\}\) satisfies \(v(t)\ge v(0)-Lt\) for every \(t\ge0\), for some \(L\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\rho>L\), \(\inf_{x\in X}P_\rho(x)=v(0)\), and every minimizer of \(P_\rho\) belongs to \(C\) and minimizes \(f\) over \(C\).

knowledge_statements.title: Perturbation-Modulus Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp open threshold obtained from secant slopes of the value function at zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\lambda_*:=\sup_{t>0}\frac{[v(0)-v(t)]_+}{t}.\] This is the least \(L\in[0,+\infty]\) satisfying \(v(t)\ge v(0)-Lt\) for all \(t\ge0\). If \(\lambda_*<+\infty\), every \(\rho>\lambda_*\) is value-exact and excludes infeasible penalized minimizers. Every \(0\le\rho<\lambda_*\) fails value exactness. Exactness at \(\rho=\lambda_*\) requires a separate equality analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The largest decrease in perturbation value per unit violation is the sharp open exactness threshold; behavior at the endpoint must be checked separately.
assumptions_latex: \(C:=\{x\in X:g(x)=0\}\) is nonempty, and \(v(t):=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\le t\}\) satisfies \(v(0)\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(\rho>\lambda_*\) is an exact penalty parameter, whereas every \(0\le\rho<\lambda_*\) fails value exactness.

notation.meaning: Least global perturbation slope governing exactness
Positive part of a real number

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\), define \[v_U(t):=\inf\{f(x):x\in U,\ g(x)\le t\},\qquad \lambda_U(\bar x):=\sup_{t>0}\frac{[f(\bar x)-v_U(t)]_+}{t}.\] If \(\lambda_U(\bar x)<+\infty\), every \(\rho>\lambda_U(\bar x)\) satisfies \[f(x)+\rho g(x)\ge f(\bar x)\quad\text{for all }x\in U.\] Hence \(\bar x\) is a local penalized minimizer, and every \(x\in U\) with \(f(x)+\rho g(x)=f(\bar x)\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite localized perturbation slope is a strict local exactness threshold and excludes infeasible points attaining the local penalized minimum value.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is a neighborhood of \(\bar x\), and \(f(\bar x)=\inf\{f(x):x\in C\cap U\}\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\rho>\lambda_U(\bar x)\), then \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(f+\rho g\), and every point in \(U\) attaining the same penalized value is feasible.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Exactness Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global threshold expressed directly through objective improvement divided by constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(\sup\varnothing:=0\), define \[\Lambda:=\sup_{\substack{x\in X,\ g(x)>0\\ f(x)<f_*}}\frac{f_*-f(x)}{g(x)}.\] If \(\Lambda<+\infty\), every \(\rho>\Lambda\) satisfies \[\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(f(x)+\rho g(x)\bigr)=f_*,\] and every attained penalized minimizer is feasible and constrained-optimal. Every \(0\le\rho<\Lambda\) fails global value exactness. The endpoint \(\rho=\Lambda\) requires separate analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The worst objective improvement per unit positive violation is the sharp open global exactness threshold; the endpoint requires a separate check.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\Lambda<+\infty\), every \(\rho>\Lambda\) is globally exact; every \(0\le\rho<\Lambda\) fails equality of the penalized and constrained infima.

children.title: Uniform Exactness Thresholds
children.top_down_role: Penalty levels valid across a prescribed family of problems or points.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Exactness Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One penalty parameter valid across an entire prescribed family of constrained problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p\in P\), define \[\Lambda(p):=\sup_{\substack{x\in X,\ g_p(x)>0\\ f_p(x)<f_p^*}}\frac{f_p^*-f_p(x)}{g_p(x)},\qquad \overline\Lambda:=\sup_{p\in P}\Lambda(p),\] with \(\sup\varnothing:=0\). The family admits a finite uniform strict exactness threshold if and only if \(\overline\Lambda<+\infty\). In that case, every \(\rho>\overline\Lambda\) is exact for every \(p\in P\), and every attained penalized minimizer is feasible. If \(\overline\Lambda=+\infty\), no finite penalty weight is exact for every member of the family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family has a finite uniform strict exactness threshold exactly when its pointwise global thresholds are uniformly bounded.
assumptions_latex: For each \(p\in P\), \(f_p:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), \(g_p:X\to[0,+\infty]\), and \(C_p:=\{x\in X:g_p(x)=0\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite \(\overline\Lambda\) is a uniform strict exactness threshold, and every \(\rho>\overline\Lambda\) is exact simultaneously for all \(p\in P\).

knowledge_statements.title: Parametric Exactness Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise threshold selection for parameterized exact-penalty problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(p\in P\), define \[\Lambda(p):=\sup_{\substack{x\in X,\ g_p(x)>0\\ f_p(x)<f_p^*}}\frac{f_p^*-f_p(x)}{g_p(x)},\] with \(\sup\varnothing:=0\). If \(\rho(p)>\Lambda(p)\), then \[\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(f_p(x)+\rho(p)g_p(x)\bigr)=f_p^*,\] and every attained penalized minimizer is feasible and constrained-optimal. If \(0\le\rho(p)<\Lambda(p)\), value exactness fails at \(p\). Exactness at equality requires a separate check.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each parameter value has its own sharp open exactness threshold, permitting pointwise selection of the penalty weight.
assumptions_latex: For each \(p\in P\), \(f_p:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), \(g_p:X\to[0,+\infty]\), and \(C_p:=\{x\in X:g_p(x)=0\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parameter-dependent penalty \(\rho(p)\) is strictly exact whenever \(\rho(p)>\Lambda(p)\); no selection with \(\rho(p)<\Lambda(p)\) is value-exact at that parameter.

knowledge_statements.title: Threshold Stability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper-semicontinuity regime ensuring persistence of a strict penalty margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\Lambda(p_0)<+\infty\) and \(\Lambda\) is upper semicontinuous at \(p_0\), then for every \(\rho>\Lambda(p_0)\) there exists a neighborhood \(V\) of \(p_0\) such that \(\rho>\Lambda(p)\) for all \(p\in V\). Therefore the same weight \(\rho\) is an exact penalty parameter throughout \(V\), and every attained penalized minimizer there is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Upper semicontinuity of a finite pointwise threshold preserves every strict penalty margin on a neighborhood of the reference parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a topological space, \(p_0\in P\), and \(\Lambda:P\to[0,+\infty]\) is the pointwise global exactness-threshold function for a parameterized family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(\rho>\Lambda(p_0)\) remains an exact penalty parameter for all parameters in some neighborhood of \(p_0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Threshold Blow-Up Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar degeneration showing threshold blow-up when violation scaling vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For this family, the open exactness threshold is \[\Lambda(p)=\frac{1}{p}.\] Thus every fixed \(p>0\) admits strictly exact penalties \(\rho>1/p\), while \(\Lambda(p)\to+\infty\) as \(p\downarrow0\). Consequently, no finite penalty parameter is uniformly exact on any parameter set containing arbitrarily small positive \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the violation scale vanishes with the parameter, the exact penalty threshold diverges and no finite uniform threshold survives near the boundary.
assumptions_latex: Strict exactness means equality of penalized and constrained optimal values together with feasibility of every attained penalized minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Although every \(p>0\) admits strictly exact penalties, \(\Lambda(p)=1/p\to+\infty\) as \(p\downarrow0\), so no finite uniform threshold exists near the degeneracy boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Minimizer Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local transfer under Lipschitz continuity and a local error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\rho\ge L\kappa\), then \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer of \(P_\rho:=f+\rho g\). If \(\rho>L\kappa\), there exists a neighborhood \(V\) of \(\bar x\) such that every \(x\in V\) satisfying \(P_\rho(x)=P_\rho(\bar x)\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local Lipschitz continuity and a local error bound transfer a constrained local minimizer to the penalty problem at weights at least their modulus product; a strict weight excludes nearby infeasible minimizers at the same value.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and closed, \(\bar x\in C\), and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to[0,+\infty]\) satisfies \(C=\{x:g(x)=0\}\).
There is a neighborhood \(U_0\) of \(\bar x\) such that \(f(\bar x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in C\cap U_0\).
The function \(f\) is finite and \(L\)-Lipschitz on a neighborhood of \(\bar x\), and \(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\kappa g(x)\) holds on a neighborhood of \(\bar x\), for constants \(L,\kappa\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\rho\ge L\kappa\), \(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(f+\rho g\); if \(\rho>L\kappa\), nearby points attaining the same penalized value are feasible.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_\rho\) has no minimizer when \(\rho<1\), every \(x\ge0\) is a global minimizer when \(\rho=1\), and \(x=0\) is its unique global minimizer when \(\rho>1\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar equality-constrained boundary example showing the sharp exact-penalty threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the constrained problem \(\min\{-x:x=0\}\), whose unique feasible minimizer is \(x=0\), and its penalty \(P_\rho(x)=-x+\rho|x|\). For \(x\ge0\), \(P_\rho(x)=(\rho-1)x\), while for \(x<0\), \(P_\rho(x)=-(1+\rho)x>0\). Hence \(\rho<1\) makes the penalized problem unbounded below; at \(\rho=1\), every \(x\ge0\) is a global minimizer, including infeasible points; and for \(\rho>1\), the constrained solution \(x=0\) is the unique global minimizer. Thus spurious minimizers occur at the threshold itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar equality problem has infeasible penalized minimizers exactly at the threshold; above it, only the constrained minimizer remains.
knowledge_statements.title: Spurious-Minimizer Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarke-stationarity transfer for a finite-dimensional equality-residual penalty with a smooth objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\lVert h(x)\rVert_1\). At any \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(h(\bar x)=0\), \[0\in\partial_C P_\rho(\bar x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists\lambda\in[-\rho,\rho]^m:\ \nabla f(\bar x)+Dh(\bar x)^\top\lambda=0.\] Consequently, a feasible equality-constrained stationary pair \((\bar x,\lambda)\) transfers to Clarke stationarity of \(P_\rho\) whenever \(\rho\ge\lVert\lambda\rVert_\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth objective and equality mapping, feasible stationarity transfers to the one-norm penalty exactly when the associated multiplier is bounded in infinity norm by the penalty weight.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f^*=\inf_{z\in C}f(z)\). For a nearest feasible point \(z\), Lipschitz continuity and the error bound imply \(f(x)\ge f(z)-L\kappa v(x)\ge f^*-L\kappa v(x)\). Therefore \(P_\rho(x)\ge f^*+(\rho-L\kappa)v(x)\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A continuously differentiable family \(F_\rho:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) is an auxiliary-variable smooth exact penalty for \(\min\{f(x):x\in C\}\) if there exists \(\bar\rho<\infty\) such that, for every \(\rho\ge\bar\rho\), \[\operatorname{proj}_X\!\left(\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in X\times Y}F_\rho(x,y)\right)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x).\] Local exactness at \(\bar x\) is defined by replacing global argmin sets with local minimizers in neighborhoods of \((\bar x,\bar y)\) and \(\bar x\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pseudo-Huber smoothing of an equality-residual one-norm penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(t\in\mathbb{R}\), \(0\le |t|-\phi_\mu(t)\le\mu\), and \(\phi_\mu(t)\to|t|\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\). Hence \[P_{\rho,\mu}(x)=f(x)+\rho\sum_{i=1}^m\left(\sqrt{c_i(x)^2+\mu^2}-\mu\right)\] satisfies \[0\le f(x)+\rho\|c(x)\|_1-P_{\rho,\mu}(x)\le\rho m\mu.\] If \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable, then \(P_{\rho,\mu}\) is continuously differentiable for every \(\mu>0\), while its pointwise limit is the nonsmooth \(\ell_1\) penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pseudo-Huber terms give a smooth equality-residual penalty lying uniformly within rho times m times mu of the nonsmooth l1 penalty.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional log-sum-exp smoothing of a maximum-violation penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[M_\mu(x)=\mu\log\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^m\exp(r_i(x)/\mu)\right).\] Then, for every \(x\), \[\max_{1\le i\le m}r_i(x)\le M_\mu(x)\le\max_{1\le i\le m}r_i(x)+\mu\log m.\] Thus \(f(x)+\rho M_\mu(x)\) uniformly approximates the maximum-violation penalty \(f(x)+\rho\max_i r_i(x)\) with error at most \(\rho\mu\log m\). If all \(r_i\) and \(f\) are continuously differentiable, the smoothed penalty is continuously differentiable for every \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Log-sum-exp smoothly approximates maximum violation, with a uniform error bounded by mu log m before multiplication by the penalty weight.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of finite exactness after smoothing an absolute-value penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every finite \(\rho\) and every \(\mu>0\), \[P'_{\rho,\mu}(0)=-1,\] so the only feasible point \(x=0\) is not stationary and cannot minimize the smooth unconstrained penalty. If \(\rho>1\), solving \(P'_{\rho,\mu}(x)=0\) gives the unique minimizer \[x_{\rho,\mu}=\frac{\mu}{\sqrt{\rho^2-1}}>0.\] If \(\rho\le1\), the penalized objective does not attain a finite exact minimizer. Thus the nonsmooth threshold \(\rho>1\) ensures exactness before smoothing, but no finite \(\rho\) restores exact feasibility while \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smoothing the scalar absolute-value penalty moves its minimizer away from feasibility for every positive smoothing parameter and every finite penalty weight.

knowledge_statements.title: Threshold Distortion under Smoothing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-dependent threshold induced by pseudo-Huber smoothing in the scalar boundary model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\rho>1\) and \(\mu>0\), the unique minimizer of \(P_{\rho,\mu}\) is \(x_{\rho,\mu}=\mu/\sqrt{\rho^2-1}\). For every tolerance \(\delta>0\), \[|x_{\rho,\mu}|\le\delta\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \rho\ge\sqrt{1+\left(\frac{\mu}{\delta}\right)^2}.\] No finite \(\rho\) gives exact feasibility when \(\mu>0\); exact feasibility is approached as \(\rho\to\infty\), while the nonsmoothed case \(\mu=0\) recovers the threshold \(\rho>1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive smoothing replaces the fixed exactness threshold by a tolerance-dependent threshold; no finite penalty weight gives exact feasibility, although feasibility is approached as the weight diverges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|x_{\rho,\mu}|\le\delta\) if and only if \(\rho\ge\sqrt{1+(\mu/\delta)^2}\); for \(\mu>0\), exact feasibility is unavailable at every finite \(\rho\).

knowledge_statements.title: Abstract MPEC Exact Penalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local exact penalization of finite-dimensional complementarity constraints under a local error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho r(x)\) for \(x\in C\). If \(\bar x\in\Omega\) is a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(\Omega\), then it is a local minimizer of \(P_\rho\) over \(C\) for every \(\rho>L\kappa\). Moreover, there is a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that every local minimizer \(x\in U\) of \(P_\rho\) over \(C\) belongs to \(\Omega\) and is a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(\Omega\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a local complementarity error bound, a penalty weight larger than the objective Lipschitz constant times the error-bound modulus transfers local minimizers in both directions near the reference solution.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i(x)\ge0\) and \(b_i(x)\ge0\) hold for every \(x\in C\) and \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
\(\bar x\in\Omega\) is a local minimizer of \(f\) over \(\Omega\), and \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on a neighborhood of \(\bar x\).
On a neighborhood of \(\bar x\) relative to \(C\), \(d(x,\Omega)\le\kappa r(x)\), and nearest points in \(\Omega\) exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\) locally minimizes \(P_\rho=f+\rho r\) over \(C\), and every sufficiently near local minimizer of \(P_\rho\) over \(C\) is feasible for the MPEC and locally minimizes \(f\) over \(\Omega\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact residual penalization of a subanalytic MPEC
knowledge_statements.scope_note: MPEC-specific equivalence between the original problem and a one-level constrained minimization problem using a fractional-power residual penalty and bounded nonnegative multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be continuous and subanalytic, \(Z\) be compact and subanalytic, and \(f\) be Lipschitz on \(Z\). Let the constraint map \(C\) be defined by functions \(g_i\) that are continuous and subanalytic, with \(g_i(x,\cdot)\) convex for every \(x\in X\). Suppose that each \(\nabla_y g_i\) exists and is continuous and subanalytic on an open set containing the MPEC feasible set \(\mathcal F\). Assume \(X\subseteq\operatorname{dom}(C)\), \(\mathcal F\neq\varnothing\), and SBCQ holds on \(\mathcal F\) for the multiplier map \(M\). Let \(c>0\) be the constant specified by the associated multiplier-bound result, and define
\[
r(x,y,\lambda)=\left\|F(x,y)+\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\lambda_i\nabla_y g_i(x,y)\right\|+\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\left((g_i(x,y))_++\lambda_i|g_i(x,y)|\right).
\]
Then there exist \(\alpha^*>0\) and an integer \(N^*>0\) such that, for every \(\alpha\geq\alpha^*\) and integer \(N\geq N^*\), \((x^*,y^*)\) solves the original MPEC if and only if there exists \(\lambda^*\in\mathbb R^\ell\) such that \((x^*,y^*,\lambda^*)\) solves
\[
\min_{(x,y,\lambda)\in Z\times(\mathbb B(0,c)\cap\mathbb R_+^\ell)} f(x,y)+\alpha r(x,y,\lambda)^{1/N}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated subanalyticity, compactness, Lipschitz continuity, convexity, differentiability, feasibility, domain, and SBCQ assumptions, sufficiently large penalty and integer root parameters make the original MPEC exactly equivalent to a one-level minimization problem with a fractional-power stationarity-and-complementarity residual and a bounded nonnegative multiplier.
assumptions_latex: g_i\text{ is continuous and subanalytic, and }g_i(x,\cdot)\text{ is convex for every }x\in X
\nabla_y g_i\text{ exists and is continuous and subanalytic on an open set containing }\mathcal F
\mathrm{SBCQ}\text{ holds on }\mathcal F\text{ for the multiplier map }M
c>0\text{ is the specified multiplier-bound constant}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\alpha^*>0\;\exists N^*\in\mathbb N_{>0}\;\forall\alpha\geq\alpha^*\;\forall N\in\mathbb N,\ N\geq N^*:\quad (x^*,y^*)\text{ solves the MPEC}\iff\exists\lambda^*\in\mathbb R^\ell:\ (x^*,y^*,\lambda^*)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y,\lambda)\in Z\times(\mathbb B(0,c)\cap\mathbb R_+^\ell)}\left[f(x,y)+\alpha r(x,y,\lambda)^{1/N}\right].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplier conditions for MPECs with piecewise-polyhedral equilibrium constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional stationarity and complementarity conditions for an affine MPEC with a piecewise-polyhedral multifunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\bar x,\bar y)\) be a local solution of the specified finite-dimensional affine MPEC. Assume \(\varphi\) is Lipschitz near \((\bar x,\bar y)\) and \(Q\) is piecewise polyhedral, meaning that \(\operatorname{gph}Q\) is a finite union of polyhedral sets. Then there exist \((x^*,y^*)\in\partial\varphi(\bar x,\bar y)\), \((u^*,v^*)\in\mathbb R^s\times\mathbb R^m\), and \(z^*=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_p)\in\mathbb R^p\) such that \[0=x^*+A_2^*u^*+A_1^*v^*+L^*z^*,\qquad 0=y^*+B_2^*u^*+B_1^*v^*+M^*z^*,\] \[u^*\in D^*Q(A_2\bar x+B_2\bar y+c_2,-A_1\bar x-B_1\bar y-c_1)(v^*),\] and, for every \(j=1,\ldots,p\), \[\lambda_j\ge0,\qquad \lambda_j\bigl((L\bar x)_j+(M\bar y)_j+e_j\bigr)=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local solution of the affine MPEC with a Lipschitz objective and piecewise-polyhedral equilibrium mapping admits subgradient and coderivative multipliers satisfying two stationarity equations and the usual nonnegativity and complementarity relations for every inequality.
assumptions_latex: (\bar x,\bar y)\text{ is a local solution of the finite-dimensional affine MPEC}
\operatorname{gph}Q\text{ is a finite union of polyhedral sets}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists(x^*,y^*,u^*,v^*,z^*):\quad \begin{cases}0=x^*+A_2^*u^*+A_1^*v^*+L^*z^*,\\0=y^*+B_2^*u^*+B_1^*v^*+M^*z^*,\\u^*\in D^*Q(\cdot)(v^*),\\\lambda_j\ge0,\ \lambda_j((L\bar x)_j+(M\bar y)_j+e_j)=0\ \forall j.\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalarized coderivative stationarity under strict Lipschitz continuity, SNC, calmness, and a nondegeneracy condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the MPEC setting with \(\bar z=-f(\bar x,\bar y)\), assume the local closedness, objective Lipschitz continuity, and calmness hypotheses for the perturbed feasible-solution mapping. Suppose additionally that \(f\) is strictly Lipschitzian at \((\bar x,\bar y)\), \(Q\) is SNC at \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar z)\), and \[(x^*,y^*)\in\bigl[\partial\langle z^*,f\rangle(\bar x,\bar y)+N((\bar x,\bar y);\Omega)\bigr]\cap\bigl[-D_N^*Q(\bar x,\bar y,\bar z)(z^*)\bigr]\] implies \(x^*=y^*=z^*=0\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Penalization-based necessary conditions for MPECs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-multiplier limiting-coderivative stationarity for equilibrium-constrained programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\bar x,\bar y)\) be a local solution of the MPEC defined by \(0\in f(x,y)+Q(x,y)\) and \((x,y)\in\Omega\), with \(f:X\times Y\to Z\) and \(Q:X\times Y\rightrightarrows Z\) between Asplund spaces. Set \(\bar z=-f(\bar x,\bar y)\). Assume \(\varphi\) is Lipschitz near \((\bar x,\bar y)\) with modulus \(\ell_\varphi\), \(f\) is continuous there, \(\Omega\) and \(\operatorname{gph}Q\) are locally closed at the reference points, the perturbation solution mapping \[G(u,v,w)=\{(x,y)\in\Omega:(u+x,v+y,w-f(x,y))\in\operatorname{gph}Q\}\] is calm at \((0,0,0,\bar x,\bar y)\) with modulus \(\ell\), \[D_M^*f(\bar x,\bar y)(0)\cap[-N((\bar x,\bar y);\Omega)]=\{0\},\] and either \(f\) is PSNC or \(\Omega\) is SNC at \((\bar x,\bar y)\). Then there exist \((x^*,y^*,z^*)\) with \(\|(x^*,y^*,z^*)\|\le\ell_\varphi\ell\) and \((x^*,y^*)\in D_N^*Q(\bar x,\bar y,\bar z)(z^*)\) such that \[(-x^*,-y^*)\in\partial\varphi(\bar x,\bar y)+D_N^*f(\bar x,\bar y)(z^*)+N((\bar x,\bar y);\Omega).\] Consequently, \[0\in\partial\varphi(\bar x,\bar y)+D_N^*f(\bar x,\bar y)(z^*)+D_N^*Q(\bar x,\bar y,\bar z)(z^*)+N((\bar x,\bar y);\Omega).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an MPEC in Asplund spaces, calmness of the perturbed feasible-solution mapping, a mixed coderivative qualification, and an SNC or PSNC assumption yield bounded multipliers satisfying limiting-coderivative stationarity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak calmness of (CP) with modulus μ
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional definition using the MPEC linearized cone of the penalized feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let  ar z=( ar x, ar y, ar u, ar v) be feasible for (CP) and let \mu>0. Problem (CP) is weakly calm at  ar z with modulus \mu if, for every d=(d_x,d_y,d_u,d_v)\in\mathcal L^{\mathrm{MPEC}}( ar z;\widetilde F), \[ [
abla F( ar x, ar y)+\mu
abla f( ar x, ar y)]^T(d_x,d_y)-\mu\min_{\xi\in W( ar x)}\xi^Td_x\ge0. \] Here \widetilde F is the feasible region of (CP_\mu), and \mathcal L^{\mathrm{MPEC}} consists of directions satisfying the linearized lower-level stationarity equation, the active upper-level inequality and equality linearizations, 
abla g_i( ar x, ar y)^T(d_x,d_y)=0 for i\in I_g, (d_u)_i=0 for i\in I_u, and, for every i\in I_0, 
abla g_i( ar x, ar y)^T(d_x,d_y)(d_u)_i=0 with 
abla g_i( ar x, ar y)^T(d_x,d_y)\le0 and (d_u)_i\ge0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak calmness with positive modulus μ means that the penalized directional derivative expression is nonnegative along every direction in the MPEC linearized cone of the penalized feasible region. That cone incorporates the linearized stationarity, active constraints, fixed multiplier directions, and biactive complementarity-direction conditions.
assumptions_latex: \bar z=(\bar x,\bar y,\bar u,\bar v)\text{ is feasible for (CP)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: [\nabla F(\bar x,\bar y)+\mu\nabla f(\bar x,\bar y)]^T(d_x,d_y)-\mu\min_{\xi\in W(\bar x)}\xi^Td_x\ge0\quad\forall d\in\mathcal L^{\mathrm{MPEC}}(\bar z;\widetilde F).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Hölder Error Bound for Nonnegative Quadratic Systems on a Polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A general quadratic-system error bound, rather than an MPEC-specific penalization result.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be a polyhedron and let $g_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, $i=1,\ldots,\ell$, be quadratic functions satisfying $g_i(x)\ge 0$ for every $x\in P$. Define $S=\{x\in P:g_i(x)=0\ \text{for all }i\}$ and $r(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}|g_i(x)|$. If $S\ne\varnothing$, then for every compact $W\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ there exists $\tau>0$ such that $\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le \tau r(x)^{1/2}$ for all $x\in P\cap W$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many quadratic functions that are nonnegative on a polyhedron, a nonempty common zero set satisfies a square-root Hölder error bound on every compact set, restricted to points in the polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\tau>0\ \forall x\in P\cap W:\quad \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le \tau\left(\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}|g_i(x)|\right)^{1/2}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ambient-Space Hölder Error Bound for Nonnegative Quadratic Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extends the polyhedron-restricted quadratic error bound to arbitrary nearby points by including distance to the polyhedron in the residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be a polyhedron and let $g_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, $i=1,\ldots,\ell$, be quadratic functions satisfying $g_i(x)\ge 0$ for every $x\in P$. Define $S=\{x\in P:g_i(x)=0\ \text{for all }i\}$ and $r(x)=\operatorname{dist}(x,P)+\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}|g_i(x)|$. If $S\ne\varnothing$, then for every compact $W\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ there exists $\tau>0$ such that $\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le \tau r(x)^{1/2}$ for every $x\in W$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty common zero set of quadratic functions that are nonnegative on a polyhedron, a square-root Hölder error bound holds for all points in any compact set when the residual also measures distance to the polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\tau>0\ \forall x\in W:\quad \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le \tau\left(\operatorname{dist}(x,P)+\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}|g_i(x)|\right)^{1/2}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact penalization of an NCP-constrained mathematical program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equivalence between an NCP-constrained program and its complementarity-product penalty reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+m}\) be compact, let \(X\) be its projection onto \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(f\) be Lipschitz on \(Z\). Suppose \(F\) satisfies the UNI-P and LIP properties, the feasible set \(\mathcal F\) of the NCP-constrained program is nonempty, and \(y+F(x,y)>0\) for every \((x,y)\in\mathcal F\). Then there exists \(\alpha^*>0\) such that, for every \(\alpha\geq\alpha^*\), a vector \((x^*,y^*)\) solves the original NCP-constrained program if and only if it solves \[\min\{f(x,y)+\alpha y^T F(x,y):(x,y)\in Z,\ y\geq0,\ F(x,y)\geq0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under compactness, Lipschitz continuity, UNI-P, LIP, nonemptiness, and strict positivity on the feasible set, every sufficiently large complementarity-product penalty parameter yields exactly the solutions of the original NCP-constrained program.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\alpha^*>0\ \forall\alpha\geq\alpha^*:\ (x^*,y^*)\text{ solves the original program}\iff (x^*,y^*)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in Z,\ y\geq0,\ F(x,y)\geq0}\bigl(f(x,y)+\alpha y^TF(x,y)\bigr).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local exactness for a generalized-equation residual penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nearest solution \(z\in S\), the assumptions imply \(f(x)\ge f(z)-L d(x,S)\) and \(r(x)\ge d(x,S)/\kappa\). Consequently, \[P_\rho(x)\ge f(z)+\left(\frac{\rho}{\kappa}-L\right)d(x,S).\] If \(\rho>L\kappa\), every local minimizer of \(f\) over \(S\) is therefore a local minimizer of \(P_\rho\). Conversely, an infeasible nearby point cannot locally minimize \(P_\rho\), because replacing it by a nearest point in \(S\) strictly lowers the penalized value. Thus nearby penalized local minimizers are feasible solutions of the variational system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variational residual becomes an exact local penalty when a metric error bound holds and the weight dominates objective variation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar t\) locally solve problem (5.69), where \(T,Z\) are Asplund spaces, \(\Omega\) is locally closed around \(\bar t\), and \(\operatorname{gph}F\) is locally closed around \((\bar t,0)\). Suppose that \(\varphi\) is locally Lipschitz around \(\bar t\) with modulus \(\ell_\varphi\), \(F^{-1}(\cdot)\cap\Omega\) is calm at \((0,\bar t)\) with modulus \(\ell\), \[D_M^*F(\bar t,0)(0)\cap[-N(\bar t;\Omega)]=\{0\},\] and either \(F\) is PSNC at \((\bar t,0)\) or \(\Omega\) is SNC at \(\bar t\). Then, for every \(\mu\ge\ell_\varphi\ell\), there exists \(z^*\in Z^*\) with \(\|z^*\|\le\mu\) such that \[0\in\partial\varphi(\bar t)+D_N^*F(\bar t,0)(z^*)+N(\bar t;\Omega).\] If \(F(t)=g(t)+\Theta\), then \[z^*\in-N(-g(\bar t);\Theta),\qquad 0\in\partial\varphi(\bar t)+D_N^*g(\bar t)(z^*)+N(\bar t;\Omega),\] provided additionally that \(g\) is continuous around \(\bar t\), \(\Theta\) is locally closed around \(-g(\bar t)\), \(D_M^*g(\bar t)(0)\cap[-N(\bar t;\Omega)]=\{0\}\), and either \(g\) is PSNC at \(\bar t\) or \(\Omega\) is SNC there.

A normal-cone specialization applies to constraints represented as a mapping plus a set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fischer–Burmeister residual as a verifiable complementarity certificate and penalty term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scalars \(u,v\), \[\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(u,v)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad u\ge0,\ v\ge0,\ uv=0.\] Therefore \[R_{\mathrm{FB}}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\left|\sqrt{a_i(x)^2+b_i(x)^2}-a_i(x)-b_i(x)\right|\] satisfies \(R_{\mathrm{FB}}(x)\ge0\), and \(R_{\mathrm{FB}}(x)=0\) if and only if \(a_i(x)\ge0\), \(b_i(x)\ge0\), and \(a_i(x)b_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\). Thus the scalar value \(R_{\mathrm{FB}}(x)\) is a directly checkable certificate of exact complementarity and can be used in \(f(x)+\rho R_{\mathrm{FB}}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The aggregate Fischer–Burmeister residual is zero exactly at complementary pairs, so its computed value certifies complementarity and supplies a penalty term.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scalar exact-penalty example exhibiting the sharp parameter threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{-x:x=0\}\), whose unique feasible minimizer is \(x^*=0\), and its absolute-value penalty \(P_\rho(x)=-x+\rho|x|\). For \(x>0\), \(P_\rho(x)=(\rho-1)x\). Hence, whenever \(0\le\rho<1\), arbitrarily small positive \(x\) satisfy \(P_\rho(x)<P_\rho(0)\), so the penalty reformulation is not locally exact at \(x^*\). At \(\rho=1\), \(P_\rho(x)\ge0=P_\rho(0)\), establishing the threshold for this family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a scalar equality constraint, every penalty parameter below one destroys local exactness; parameter one is the sharp threshold.

knowledge_statements.title: Exactness Failure under Irregular Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of an absolute-value exact penalty for the nonregular equality mapping h(x)=x^2.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{x:h(x)=0\}\) with \(h(x)=x^2\). The feasible set is \(\{0\}\), so \(x^*=0\) is the unique constrained minimizer. For finite \(\rho\ge 0\), define the absolute-value penalty \(P_\rho(x)=x+\rho|h(x)|=x+\rho x^2\). Then \(x^*=0\) is not a local minimizer of \(P_\rho\) for any finite \(\rho\). Thus this irregular equality admits no finite exact absolute-value penalty parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the irregular equality h(x)=x-squared, no finite absolute-value penalty parameter makes the unique feasible minimizer a local minimizer of the penalized objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No finite absolute-value penalty parameter makes \(x^*=0\) a local minimizer of \(P_\rho\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scalar example separating penalty stationarity from feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the constrained problem \(\min\{(x-1)^2:x=0\}\), define \(P_\rho(x)=(x-1)^2+\rho|x|\). If \(0<\rho<2\), then on \((0,\infty)\) the function is differentiable and \(P_\rho'(x)=2(x-1)+\rho\). Consequently \(x_\rho=1-\rho/2>0\) satisfies \(P_\rho'(x_\rho)=0\), and indeed is the minimizer of the positive smooth branch. Since the original equality requires \(x=0\), this stationary penalty point is infeasible. Thus stationarity of a finite-parameter nonsmooth penalty does not by itself certify feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite absolute-value penalty can possess a smooth stationary point that violates the original constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible Stationary Penalty Points

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning degradation for a linear equality under quadratic penalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P_\rho(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2+\tfrac\rho2(a^{\mathsf T}x)^2\), the Hessian is \(H_\rho=I+\rho aa^{\mathsf T}\). Its eigenvalue along \(a\) is \(1+\rho\|a\|_2^2\), while every vector orthogonal to \(a\) has eigenvalue \(1\). Therefore \(\kappa_2(H_\rho)=1+\rho\|a\|_2^2\). Although increasing \(\rho\) enforces the equality \(a^{\mathsf T}x=0\) more strongly, it makes Newton systems and local quadratic models increasingly ill-conditioned.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional KKT residual map using the minimum complementarity function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every $(x,\mu,\lambda)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+\ell+m}$, $\operatorname{Jac}\Phi_{\min}(x,\mu,\lambda)$ is the family of matrices
\[
\begin{bmatrix}
J_x\mathbf L(x,\mu,\lambda)&Jh(x)^T&Jg(x)^T\\
-Jh(x)&0&0\\
-D_a(x,\lambda)Jg(x)&0&D_b(x,\lambda)
\end{bmatrix},
\]
where $D_a=\operatorname{diag}(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$, with $a_i=1$ for $i\in\alpha(x,\lambda)$, $a_i\in\{0,1\}$ for $i\in\beta(x,\lambda)$, and $a_i=0$ for $i\in\gamma(x,\lambda)$, and where $D_b=I_m-D_a$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At any primal-dual triple, the limiting Jacobian of the minimum-function KKT residual consists exactly of the displayed block matrices. The diagonal selector equals one on alpha indices, zero on gamma indices, and may independently equal zero or one on beta indices; the complementary diagonal block is the identity minus this selector.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear NCP merit coercivity characterized by R0 matrices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine NCP map; covers both minimum-map and Fischer–Burmeister merit functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=q+Mx\), where \(q\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\). Then \(\theta_{\min}\), equivalently \(\theta_{\mathrm{FB}}\), is coercive on \(\mathbb R^n\) if and only if \(M\) is an \(R_0\)-matrix. This holds in particular if (a) \(M\) is nondegenerate, (b) \(M\) is strictly semicopositive, or (c) for every nonempty \(\alpha\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), there exists \(y_\alpha\) such that \(y_\alpha^TM_{\alpha\alpha}>0\) componentwise.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \theta_{\min}\text{ and }\theta_{\mathrm{FB}}\text{ are coercive}\iff M\text{ is }R_0;\quad (a),(b),\text{ or }(c)\implies M\text{ is }R_0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mesh-independent local convergence without uniform growth conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semismooth Newton method for the discrete equations \(\Phi_{2h}(u_h)=0\), including the continuous case \(h=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose Algorithm 6.27 is applied to \(\Phi_{2h}(u_h)=0\), Assumption 6.19 holds with \(r=2\), and Assumption 6.28 holds. Let \(\bar z=Z(\bar u)\), and assume that for some \(C,\gamma,t_0>0\), \[\operatorname{meas}\{\omega:0<|\bar z(\omega)|<t\}\le Ct^\gamma\quad(0<t\le t_0),\qquad \operatorname{meas}\{\omega:\bar z(\omega)=0\}=0.\] Then, for all sufficiently small meshes, \(\|\bar z_h-\bar z\|_{L^p}<\delta'\), where \(\delta'=\min\{1,(t_0/2)^{(p+\gamma)/p}\}\) for \(p<\infty\) and \(\delta'=\min\{1,t_0/2\}\) for \(p=\infty\). With \(C_Z=C_{G'}/[\lambda_0(1+\kappa)]\), \(L_Z=L_G/\lambda_0\), \[\theta=\begin{cases}\gamma(p-2)/[2(p+\gamma)],&p<\infty,\\ \gamma/2,&p=\infty,\end{cases}\quad C_N=\begin{cases}\max\{1,(2^\gamma C)^{(p-2)/(2p)}\}L_Z,&p<\infty,\\ \sqrt{3^\gamma C}\,L_Z,&p=\infty,\end{cases}\] and \(\delta''=\min\{\delta'/L_Z,\delta_0\}\), every iterate satisfying \(\|u_h^k-\bar u_h\|_{L^2}<\delta''\) obeys \[\|u_h^{k+1}-\bar u_h\|_{L^2}\le C_MC_N\max\{\|\bar z_h-\bar z\|_{L^p},L_Z\|u_h^k-\bar u_h\|_{L^2}\}^{\theta}\|u_h^k-\bar u_h\|_{L^2}+C_MC_Z\|u_h^k-\bar u_h\|_{L^2}^{1+\kappa}.\] Consequently, for every \(\eta\in(0,1)\), sufficiently fine meshes and sufficiently close initial iterates yield convergence to \(\bar u_h\) at least \(q\)-linearly with rate \(\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the cited discretization assumptions, a power-law bound on the measure of the near-zero set of the switching function, and strict complementarity, sufficiently fine discretizations satisfy a uniform local semismooth Newton error estimate. Hence, for any prescribed rate between zero and one, all sufficiently close initial iterates converge at least q-linearly with that rate, uniformly for sufficiently small mesh sizes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\eta\in(0,1)\ \exists\delta>0,\ h_2>0\ \forall h\le h_2:\ \|u_h^0-\bar u_h\|_{L^2}<\delta\Longrightarrow u_h^k\to\bar u_h\text{ at least }q\text{-linearly with rate }\eta,\text{ with the stated one-step estimate}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: MPCC model and penalized minimum-residual formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a general mathematical program with complementarity constraints and its nonsmooth residual-penalty representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \mathcal Z\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+2m} be closed and convex, F:\mathbb{R}^{n+2m}\to\mathbb{R}^k, and G:\mathbb{R}^{n+2m}\to\mathbb{R}^{\ell}. A general MPCC has the form
\[
\min_{(x,y,z)\in\mathcal Z}\theta(x,y,z)\quad\text{s.t.}\quad F(x,y,z)\le0,\quad G(x,y,z)=0,\quad 0\le y\perp z\ge0.
\]
Using \min\{y,z\} as the complementarity residual gives the penalty formulation
\[
\min_{(x,y,z)\in\mathcal Z}\theta(x,y,z)+\rho\bigl(\|\max\{F(x,y,z),0\}\|+\|G(x,y,z)\|+\|\min\{y,z\}\|\bigr).
\]
For exact-penalty purposes, the residual terms are measured with a polyhedral norm such as \ell_1 or \ell_\infty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An MPCC minimizes an objective over a closed convex set subject to inequality, equality, and componentwise complementarity constraints. Replacing each constraint family by its residual produces a nonsmooth penalty model; polyhedral norms are used for exact-penalty formulations.
assumptions_latex: \|\cdot\|\text{ is polyhedral when exact penalization is sought}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le y\perp z\ge0\text{ is represented by }\min\{y,z\}=0,\text{ yielding the stated residual-penalty MPCC formulation.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Min-Based Newton Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Newton iteration for the complementarity equation \(\min(F(x),G(x))=0\), with the minimum understood componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x^0\in\mathbb R^n\), for \(k=0,1,\ldots\), stop if \(\min(F(x^k),G(x^k))=0\). Otherwise choose \(A^k\in\mathcal A_{\min}(x^k)\), solve \(\min(F(x^k),G(x^k))+A^k d^k=0\), and set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+d^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from any point, stop when the componentwise minimum complementarity residual vanishes. Otherwise select an admissible generalized derivative matrix, solve its Newton linearization for a direction, and take the full step.
assumptions_latex: \min(F(x^k),G(x^k))+A^k d^k=0\text{ is solvable at each nonterminal iteration}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^{k+1}=x^k+d^k\quad\text{until}\quad \min(F(x^k),G(x^k))=0

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional derivative of the binary minimum function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional derivative of the scalar minimum of two real arguments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\theta:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}\) be defined by \(\theta(u,v)=\min\{u,v\}\). For every \((u,v),(d_u,d_v)\in\mathbb{R}^2\),
\[
\theta'((u,v);(d_u,d_v))=
\begin{cases}
d_u,&u<v,\\
\min\{d_u,d_v\},&u=v,\\
d_v,&v<u.
\end{cases}
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The directional derivative follows the direction of the uniquely smaller argument; when the arguments are equal, it is the minimum of the two directional components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \theta'((u,v);(d_u,d_v))=\begin{cases}d_u,&u<v,\\ \min\{d_u,d_v\},&u=v,\\ d_v,&v<u.\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mesh-independent local convergence of the smoothed semismooth Newton method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semismooth Newton method with smoothing step for \(\Phi_{1h}(u_h)=0\), including the continuous case \(h=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose Algorithm 6.26 is applied to \(\Phi_{1h}(u_h)=0\), Assumption 6.19 holds with \(r=p\), and Assumptions 6.28 and 6.24 hold. Assume that, uniformly for sufficiently small \(h\), \(\|\lambda_h\|_{L^\infty}\le\lambda_1\) and \(\|\sigma_h\|_{L^\infty}\le\sigma_1\), where \(\lambda_1,\sigma_1>0\). Let \(\bar z=\widehat Z(\bar u)\), and suppose for some \(C,\gamma,t_0>0\), \[\operatorname{meas}\{\omega:0<|\bar z(\omega)|<t\}\le Ct^\gamma\quad(0<t\le t_0),\qquad \operatorname{meas}\{\omega:\bar z(\omega)=0\}=0.\] Then, for sufficiently small \(h\), \(\|\bar z_h-\bar z\|_{L^p}<\delta'\), with \(\delta'=\min\{1,(t_0/2)^{(p+\gamma)/p}\}\) for \(p<\infty\) and \(\delta'=\min\{1,t_0/2\}\) for \(p=\infty\). There exist \(\delta_0'\ge\delta_0/\operatorname{meas}(\Omega)^{(p-2)/(2p)}\) and \(L_p\le\operatorname{meas}(\Omega)^{(p-2)/(2p)}L_G\) (with exponent \(1/2\) when \(p=\infty\)) such that the relevant \(L^p\)-ball lies in the \(L^2\)-ball and \([G_h]_{p,p}\) is Lipschitz there with modulus \(L_p\). Define \[C_{\widehat Z}=\frac{\sigma_1C_{G'}}{1+\kappa},\quad L_{\widehat Z}=\sup_{h\le h_1}\bigl(\|\sigma_h\lambda_h-1\|_{L^\infty}+\|\sigma_h\|_{L^\infty}L_p\bigr),\] \[\theta=\begin{cases}\gamma(p-2)/[2(p+\gamma)],&p<\infty,\\ \gamma/2,&p=\infty,\end{cases}\quad C_N=\begin{cases}\max\{1,(2^\gamma C)^{(p-2)/(2p)}\}L_{\widehat Z},&p<\infty,\\ \sqrt{3^\gamma C}\,L_{\widehat Z},&p=\infty.\end{cases}\] With \(\delta''=\min\{\delta'/L_{\widehat Z},\delta_0'\}\), every iterate satisfying \(\|u_h^k-\bar u_h\|_{L^p}<\delta''\) obeys \[\|u_h^{k+1}-\bar u_h\|_{L^p}\le C_NC_ML_S\max\{\|\bar z_h-\bar z\|_{L^p},L_{\widehat Z}\|u_h^k-\bar u_h\|_{L^p}\}^{\theta}\|u_h^k-\bar u_h\|_{L^p}+C_{\widehat Z}C_ML_S\|u_h^k-\bar u_h\|_{L^p}^{1+\kappa}.\] Consequently, for every \(\eta\in(0,1)\), sufficiently fine meshes and sufficiently close \(L^p\) initial iterates yield convergence to \(\bar u_h\) at least \(q\)-linearly with rate \(\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the cited discretization and smoothing assumptions, uniform bounds on the smoothing coefficients, a power-law estimate for the near-zero set of the switching function, and strict complementarity, the smoothed semismooth Newton iteration satisfies a mesh-uniform local error estimate in the Lp norm. Any desired q-linear rate below one follows for sufficiently fine meshes and sufficiently close initial iterates.
assumptions_latex: \text{Assumption 6.19 holds with }r=p\text{, and Assumptions 6.28 and 6.24 hold}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\eta\in(0,1)\ \exists\delta>0,\ h_2>0\ \forall h\le h_2:\ \|u_h^0-\bar u_h\|_{L^p}<\delta\Longrightarrow u_h^k\to\bar u_h\text{ in }L^p\text{ at least }q\text{-linearly with rate }\eta,\text{ with the stated one-step estimate}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: H-matrix lower bound for the complementarity constant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit positive lower bound for \(c(M)\) obtained from the comparison matrix of an H-matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

\[

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Horizon Functions of Pointwise Suprema and Infima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Calculus rules and equality regimes for horizon functions under pointwise extrema.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For functions $f_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}$, $i\in I$, one has $(\sup_{i\in I}f_i)^\infty\ge\sup_{i\in I}f_i^\infty$ and $(\inf_{i\in I}f_i)^\infty\le\inf_{i\in I}f_i^\infty$. The first inequality is equality when $\sup_{i\in I}f_i$ is not identically $+\infty$ and every $f_i$ is convex, lsc, and proper. The second inequality is equality whenever $I$ is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The horizon of a pointwise supremum dominates the supremum of the individual horizons, while the horizon of a pointwise infimum is bounded above by their infimum. Convex closed proper data give equality for a nontrivial supremum, and finiteness of the index set gives equality for the infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left(\sup_{i\in I}f_i\right)^\infty\ge\sup_{i\in I}f_i^\infty,\qquad\left(\inf_{i\in I}f_i\right)^\infty\le\inf_{i\in I}f_i^\infty,\quad\text{with the stated equality regimes.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum-equation representation of multi-vertical complementarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation of finite-family componentwise complementarity as a nonsmooth minimum equation; canonical ownership of the problem class is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F^i:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) for \(i=1,\ldots,r\). Then \[\min\{F^1(x),\ldots,F^r(x)\}=0,\] with componentwise minimum, if and only if \[F^i(x)\geq0\quad(i=1,\ldots,r),\qquad \forall j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\ \exists i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}:F_j^i(x)=0.\] Thus the multi-vertical complementarity conditions admit an equivalent nonsmooth minimum-equation representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The componentwise minimum of a finite family of vector mappings equals zero exactly when every mapping value is componentwise nonnegative and, in each component, at least one family member vanishes. This represents multi-vertical complementarity as a nonsmooth equation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularity of a Min-Complementarity Constraint System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity at a feasible solution of a smooth system containing inequalities, equalities, and a componentwise min-complementarity constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\) solve \(g(x)\le 0\), \(h(x)=0\), and \(\min\{G(x),H(x)\}=0\), where the minimum is componentwise. The system is regular at \(\bar x\) if zero is a regular value of the active equality system formed by \(g_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\) with \(g_i(\bar x)=0\), \(h(x)=0\), \(G_j(x)=0\) for every \(j\) with \(G_j(\bar x)=0\), and \(H_j(x)=0\) for every \(j\) with \(H_j(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a solution, an inequality-equality system with componentwise min-complementarity constraints is called regular when zero is a regular value of the equation system consisting of all active inequality components, all equality components, and all active components from both sides of the min constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\text{ is a regular value of }x\mapsto\bigl((g_i(x))_{i:g_i(\bar x)=0},h(x),(G_j(x))_{j:G_j(\bar x)=0},(H_j(x))_{j:H_j(\bar x)=0}\bigr).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasi-Regular Primal-Dual Triple
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition for a minimum-function KKT residual with equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A triple $(x,\mu,\lambda)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+\ell+m}$ is quasi-regular if, for every subset $\mathcal J\subseteq\beta(x,\lambda)$, the matrix
\[
M_{\min}(\mathcal J)=
\begin{bmatrix}
J_x\mathbf L(x,\mu,\lambda)&Jh(x)^T&Jg_{\alpha}(x)^T&Jg_{\mathcal J}(x)^T\\
-Jh(x)&0&0&0\\
-Jg_{\alpha}(x)&0&0&0\\
-Jg_{\mathcal J}(x)&0&0&0
\end{bmatrix}
\]
is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual triple is quasi-regular when every indicated KKT matrix obtained by selecting an arbitrary subset of the beta index set is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x,\mu,\lambda)\text{ is quasi-regular}\iff \forall\mathcal J\subseteq\beta(x,\lambda),\ M_{\min}(\mathcal J)\text{ is nonsingular}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The natural residual map for the nonlinear complementarity problem associated with \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is \[R_{\mathrm{nat}}(x)=\min\{x,F(x)\},\] where the minimum is taken componentwise. Thus \((R_{\mathrm{nat}}(x))_i=\min\{x_i,F_i(x)\}\). Its zero equation is equivalent to the complementarity system \[x\ge0,\qquad F(x)\ge0,\qquad x_iF_i(x)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).\] The norm \(\|R_{\mathrm{nat}}(x)\|\) is therefore a residual measure whose vanishing characterizes solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The natural residual is the componentwise minimum of x and F(x), and it vanishes exactly at complementarity solutions.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_K(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\in K\) and \(\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\ge0\) for all \(y\in K\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean metric projection onto the closed convex set.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Pi_K(z)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in K}\|y-z\|_2\), which is single-valued for nonempty closed convex \(K\). Define \[R_K(x)=x-\Pi_K(x-F(x)).\] Then \(R_K(x)=0\) if and only if \(x=\Pi_K(x-F(x))\). By the projection optimality condition, this fixed-point equation is equivalent to \[x\in K\quad\text{and}\quad \langle F(x),y-x\rangle\ge0\quad\text{for every }y\in K.\] Thus zeros of the projection residual coincide with solutions of the variational inequality on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variational inequality solution is exactly a fixed point of projection after a negative F step, or equivalently a zero of the projection residual.

children.top_down_role: Regimes linking residual formulations to projection formulations.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(x-\Pi_K(x-F(x))=\min\{x,F(x)\}\) componentwise.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the nonnegative orthant.

source_refs.locator: 10.1.2 Using the min function p. 909

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\mathbb R_+^n\), the Euclidean projection is \((\Pi_K(z))_i=\max\{z_i,0\}\). Consequently, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \[x-\Pi_K(x-F(x))=\min\{x,F(x)\}=R_{\mathrm{nat}}(x),\] with all operations interpreted componentwise. Therefore the projection residual and natural residual are identical in the orthant, unit-step regime; in particular, their zero sets and residual norms coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the nonnegative orthant with a unit step, the projection residual equals the componentwise minimum residual exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual–Projection Equivalence Regimes

children.title: Projection Regularity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Geometric regimes where projection-based regularity deteriorates.

assumptions_latex: Metric projection is taken in Euclidean distance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Closed convexity ensures a single-valued nonexpansive projection, whereas closed nonconvex sets can have multivalued projections.

notation.meaning: Possibly set-valued metric projection onto a set.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity boundary for single-valued, nonexpansive Euclidean projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, then \(\Pi_K\) is single-valued and nonexpansive: \[\|\Pi_K(u)-\Pi_K(v)\|_2\le\|u-v\|_2\quad\text{for all }u,v\in\mathbb R^n.\] Closedness without convexity does not ensure a projection map. For \(K_0=\{-1,1\}\subset\mathbb R\), both points minimize the distance from \(0\), so \(\Pi_{K_0}(0)=\{-1,1\}\). Hence a residual written using an unqualified projection can become set-valued, and smooth or semismooth map-based analysis no longer follows automatically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex closed sets have single-valued nonexpansive projections; a closed nonconvex two-point set already yields a multivalued projection.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Regularity Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex/nonconvex boundary and two-point example are correct, but no citation is supplied. The phrase that nonconvex closedness does not ensure a projection map should be understood as failure of a single-valued projection map; nearest points still exist for nonempty closed subsets of finite-dimensional Euclidean space.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mu>0\), define \[m_\mu(a,b)=\frac{a+b-\sqrt{(a-b)^2+4\mu^2}}{2}.\] This function is continuously differentiable, indeed smooth, in \((a,b)\). Since \(\min\{a,b\}=\tfrac12(a+b-|a-b|)\), \[0\le\min\{a,b\}-m_\mu(a,b)=\frac{\sqrt{(a-b)^2+4\mu^2}-|a-b|}{2}\le\mu.\] Therefore \(m_\mu\) converges uniformly to \(\min\{a,b\}\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\), and its componentwise extension smooths the minimum complementarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A square-root formula smoothly underestimates the minimum by at most the smoothing parameter and converges uniformly as that parameter vanishes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Square-root smoothing with perturbed complementarity product \(ab=\mu^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the classical Fischer–Burmeister smoothing by \[\phi_\mu(a,b)=\sqrt{a^2+b^2+2\mu^2}-a-b.\] For each \(\mu>0\), \(\phi_\mu\) is smooth on \(\mathbb R^2\), and \[\phi_\mu(a,b)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a>0,\ b>0,\ ab=\mu^2.\] Furthermore, with \(\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(a,b)=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}-a-b\), \[0\le\phi_\mu(a,b)-\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(a,b)\le\sqrt{2}\,\mu.\] Hence \(\phi_\mu\) converges uniformly to the Fischer–Burmeister function as \(\mu\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical Fischer–Burmeister smoothing replaces exact complementarity by a positive product equal to the squared smoothing parameter and converges uniformly.
knowledge_statements.title: Classical Fischer–Burmeister Smoothing

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mu>0\), define the regularized Fischer–Burmeister function by \(\phi_\mu(a,b)=\sqrt{a^2+b^2+2\mu^2}-a-b\) for \((a,b)\in\mathbb R^2\). It is continuously differentiable and satisfies \(\phi_\mu(a,b)\to\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(a,b)=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}-a-b\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\). Moreover, \(\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(a,b)=0\) is equivalent to \(a\ge0\), \(b\ge0\), and \(ab=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regularized Fischer–Burmeister function smoothly approximates the Fischer–Burmeister complementarity equation and converges to it as the positive regularization parameter vanishes; the limiting zero equation is equivalent to nonnegative complementarity.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mu>0\), the Chen–Harker–Kanzow–Smale smoothing of the minimum function is \(m_\mu(a,b)=\tfrac12\bigl(a+b-\sqrt{(a-b)^2+4\mu^2}\bigr)\). The map is continuously differentiable on \(\mathbb R^2\) and obeys \(m_\mu(a,b)\to\min\{a,b\}\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\). Hence the limiting equation \(m_0(a,b)=0\) is equivalent to \(a\ge0\), \(b\ge0\), and \(ab=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CHKS replaces the scalar minimum by a smooth square-root formula whose zero equation approaches nonnegative complementarity as the smoothing parameter vanishes.
knowledge_statements.title: CHKS Smoothing Functions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convolution-based smoothing of the positive-part and minimum functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho:\mathbb R\to[0,\infty)\) be a probability density with finite first absolute moment. For \(\mu>0\), define \(p_\mu(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}(t-\mu s)_+\rho(s)\,ds\) and \(m_\mu(a,b)=a-p_\mu(a-b)\). If \(\rho\) is continuous, then \(p_\mu\) and \(m_\mu\) are continuously differentiable. Furthermore, \(p_\mu(t)\to t_+\) and \(m_\mu(a,b)\to\min\{a,b\}\) as \(\mu\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Chen–Mangasarian smoothing convolves the positive-part function with a scaled density, thereby producing a continuously differentiable approximation of the scalar minimum under the stated kernel assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Chen–Mangasarian Smoothing Functions

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be locally Lipschitz. A family \(F_\mu:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), \(\mu>0\), is a strong smoothing of \(F\) if every \(F_\mu\) is continuously differentiable and, for each compact \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\), there exist \(c_K>0\) and \(\bar\mu_K>0\) such that \(\sup_{x\in K}\|F_\mu(x)-F(x)\|\le c_K\mu\) whenever \(0<\mu\le\bar\mu_K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strong smoothing is continuously differentiable for positive parameter and approximates the original locally Lipschitz mapping with uniform first-order error on every compact set.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be locally Lipschitz and let \(F_\mu\) be continuously differentiable for \(\mu>0\). The smoothing is Jacobian-consistent at \(x\) if \[\lim_{\substack{z\to x\\ \mu\downarrow0}}\operatorname{dist}\!\left(\nabla F_\mu(z),\partial_C F(x)\right)=0,\] where distance is induced by a matrix norm. It is Jacobian-consistent on a set \(D\) when this condition holds at every \(x\in D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jacobian consistency requires every nearby limiting smoothed Jacobian to approach the Clarke generalized Jacobian of the original mapping.
knowledge_statements.title: Jacobian-Consistent Smoothing Functions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Descent of the Centered Newton Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descent property under the strict radial-growth and potential-gradient alignment conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose (IP5) and (IP6) hold. If \(x\in X_{\mathcal I}\), \(d\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\sigma\in[0,\bar\sigma)\) satisfy \(G(x)\ne0\) and \[G(x)+JG(x)d=\sigma\frac{a^TG(x)}{\|a\|^2}a,\] then \(\nabla\psi(G(x))^Td<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under conditions IP5 and IP6, any direction satisfying the centered Newton equation at an interior point with nonzero residual is a strict descent direction in the stated potential-gradient sense, provided the centering parameter is at least zero and strictly below bar-sigma.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interior Potential-Reduction Newton Algorithm with Backtracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton iteration using a centered Jacobian equation and dyadic Armijo backtracking while preserving membership in the interior set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x^0\in X_{\mathcal I}\), \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), and \(\{\sigma_k\}\subset[0,\bar\sigma)\). At iteration \(k\), stop if \(G(x^k)=0\). Otherwise solve \[G(x^k)+JG(x^k)d^k=\sigma_k\frac{a^TG(x^k)}{\|a\|^2}a,\] taking the right-hand side to be zero when \(a=0\). Choose the smallest \(i_k\in\mathbb Z_+\) such that \(x^k+2^{-i_k}d^k\in X_{\mathcal I}\) and \[\psi(x^k+2^{-i_k}d^k)-\psi(x^k)\le\gamma 2^{-i_k}\nabla\psi(x^k)^Td^k.\] Set \(\tau_k=2^{-i_k}\) and \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\tau_kd^k\), then repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from an interior point, stop at a zero of G. Otherwise compute a Newton direction from the centered Jacobian equation, with a zero right-hand side when a is zero. Use the first dyadic step that remains in the interior and satisfies the Armijo decrease inequality for psi, update the iterate, and repeat.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\tau_kd^k\), where \(\tau_k=2^{-i_k}\) is the first interior-feasible dyadic step satisfying the stated Armijo inequality; the algorithm terminates when \(G(x^k)=0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smoothing Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterized smooth approximation of a finite-valued nonsmooth function on Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi_0:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be nonsmooth. A function \(\varphi:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R_+\to\mathbb R\) is a smoothing function of \(\varphi_0\) if: (i) \(\varphi\) is continuous and \(\varphi(\cdot,\mu)\) is continuously differentiable for every \(\mu>0\); and (ii), for every \(w\in\mathbb R^n\), \[\lim_{\widetilde w\to w,\,\mu\to0+}\varphi(\widetilde w,\mu)=\varphi_0(w).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smoothing function is jointly continuous, is continuously differentiable in the decision variable for every positive smoothing parameter, and converges to the nonsmooth target under simultaneous convergence of the decision point and parameter to the target point and zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varphi\text{ is a smoothing function of }\varphi_0\iff\bigl[(i)\text{ and }(ii)\text{ hold}\bigr].

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(F(u)=\lambda u+G(u)\) with \(\lambda>0\), and let \(S\) be the mapping defined by the smoothing construction. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationarity and Local Convergence of a Jacobian-Consistent Smoothing Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accumulation-point stationarity and conditional convergence-rate guarantees for Algorithm 11.8.6.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n$ be locally Lipschitz continuous, let $G_\varepsilon$ be a smoothing of $G$, and suppose Algorithm 11.8.6 produces an infinite sequence $\{x^k\}$. Assume $G_\varepsilon$ is Jacobian consistent at every limit point of $\{x^k\}$. Then every accumulation point $x^\infty$ of $\{x^k\}$ is C-stationary for $\theta$. If, in addition, $G(x^\infty)=0$, $\partial G(x^\infty)$ is nonsingular, $G$ is semismooth at $x^\infty$, and $G_\varepsilon$ approximates $G$ superlinearly at $x^\infty$, then the entire sequence converges to $x^\infty$ Q-superlinearly. Under strong semismoothness and quadratic approximation in place of the corresponding assumptions, the convergence is Q-quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under local Lipschitz continuity and Jacobian consistency, every accumulation point generated by the smoothing algorithm is C-stationary. If that accumulation point is a zero, its generalized Jacobian is nonsingular, and the stated semismoothness and smoothing-approximation conditions hold, the entire sequence converges to it Q-superlinearly, or Q-quadratically under the strengthened paired conditions.
assumptions_latex: \{x^k\}\text{ is an infinite sequence produced by Algorithm 11.8.6}
G_\varepsilon\text{ is Jacobian consistent at every limit point of }\{x^k\}
x^\infty\text{ is an accumulation point of }\{x^k\}
G(x^\infty)=0\text{ and }\partial G(x^\infty)\text{ is nonsingular for the convergence-rate conclusions}
G\text{ is semismooth at }x^\infty\text{ and }G_\varepsilon\text{ approximates }G\text{ superlinearly there for Q-superlinear convergence}
G\text{ is strongly semismooth at }x^\infty\text{ and }G_\varepsilon\text{ approximates }G\text{ quadratically there for Q-quadratic convergence}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\infty\text{ is C-stationary for }\theta;\quad x^k\to x^\infty\text{ Q-superlinearly, or Q-quadratically under the strengthened paired assumptions.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smoothing of a Locally Lipschitz Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterized smooth approximation on a prescribed domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n$ be locally Lipschitz, let $\mathcal P\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ contain $0$ and a sequence of nonzero vectors converging to $0$, and let $\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n$. A family $\{G_\varepsilon:\varepsilon\in\mathcal P\}$ is a smoothing of $G$ on $\mathcal D$ if every $G_\varepsilon:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n$ is continuously differentiable on $\mathcal D$, $(\varepsilon,x)\mapsto G_\varepsilon(x)$ is continuous on $\mathcal P\times\mathcal D$, and $G_0(x)=G(x)$ for every $x\in\mathcal D$. Each $G_\varepsilon$ is a smoothing function on $\mathcal D$; if $\mathcal D$ is a neighborhood of $\bar x$, it is a smoothing near $\bar x$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smoothing is a parameterized family of mappings that is continuously differentiable in the point, jointly continuous in parameter and point, and equals the original locally Lipschitz mapping at parameter zero.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal P\subseteq\mathbb R^m\text{ contains }0\text{ and a sequence of nonzero vectors converging to }0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{G_\varepsilon\}_{\varepsilon\in\mathcal P}\text{ is a smoothing on }\mathcal D\iff \bigl[G_\varepsilon\in C^1(\mathcal D)\ \forall\varepsilon\in\mathcal P,\ (\varepsilon,x)\mapsto G_\varepsilon(x)\text{ is continuous},\ G_0|_{\mathcal D}=G|_{\mathcal D}\bigr].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Properties of the squared smoothed Fischer–Burmeister function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the nonsmooth boundary case at smoothing parameter zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the function \(\psi_{\mathrm{FB}_\mu}\): (a) \(\psi_{\mathrm{FB}_\mu}^2\in C^1(\mathbb R^2)\) for every \(\mu\ge0\). (b) If \(\mu>0\), then for every \((a,b)\in\mathbb R^2\) and every unit \(x\in\mathbb R^2\), \(\left|x^T\nabla^2\psi_{\mathrm{FB}_\mu}^2(a,b)x\right|\le2(9+\sqrt2)\); for \(\mu=0\), this holds whenever \((a,b)\ne(0,0)\). (c) For \(\mu_1,\mu_2\ge0\), \(\left|\psi_{\mathrm{FB}_{\mu_1}}^2(a,b)-\psi_{\mathrm{FB}_{\mu_2}}^2(a,b)\right|\le(2+\sqrt2)|\mu_1-\mu_2|\). (d) For \(\mu\ge0\), \(\frac{2}{2+\sqrt2}\min(a,b)^2-(2+\sqrt2)\mu\le\psi_{\mathrm{FB}_\mu}^2(a,b)\le(2+\sqrt2)\min(a,b)^2+(2+\sqrt2)\mu\). (e) If \(\mu>0\), then \(-2<\partial_a\psi_{\mathrm{FB}_\mu}(a,b)<0\), \(-2<\partial_b\psi_{\mathrm{FB}_\mu}(a,b)<0\), and \((\partial_a\psi_{\mathrm{FB}_\mu})^2+(\partial_b\psi_{\mathrm{FB}_\mu})^2\ge3-2\sqrt2>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The squared smoothed Fischer–Burmeister function is continuously differentiable, has uniformly bounded Hessian away from the zero-parameter singular point, is Lipschitz in the smoothing parameter, is bounded above and below by multiples of the squared minimum residual with an additive smoothing error, and has strictly negative, nonvanishing component derivatives for positive smoothing parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \psi_{\mathrm{FB}_\mu}^2\text{ satisfies properties (a)--(e) above.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak and Strong Jacobian Consistency of a Smoothing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential consistency of smoothing Jacobians with generalized Jacobians at a reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n$ be locally Lipschitz and let $G_\varepsilon$ be a smoothing of $G$ near $\bar x$. It is weakly Jacobian consistent at $\bar x$ if, for every $x^k\to\bar x$ and every $\varepsilon_k\in\mathcal P$ with $\varepsilon_k\to0$, the sequence $\{JG_{\varepsilon_k}(x^k)\}$ has at least one accumulation point and every such point belongs to $\partial_CG(\bar x)$. It is Jacobian consistent at $\bar x$ if every such accumulation point belongs to the smaller set $\partial G(\bar x)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak Jacobian consistency requires every vanishing-parameter sequence of nearby smoothing Jacobians to have an accumulation point, with all such points in the Clarke generalized Jacobian. Jacobian consistency strengthens membership to the smaller generalized-Jacobian set.
assumptions_latex: G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\text{ is locally Lipschitz}
G_\varepsilon\text{ is a smoothing of }G\text{ near }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Limsup}_{k\to\infty}JG_{\varepsilon_k}(x^k)\neq\varnothing,\qquad \operatorname{Limsup}_{k\to\infty}JG_{\varepsilon_k}(x^k)\subseteq\partial_CG(\bar x),\quad\text{or, for Jacobian consistency, }\subseteq\partial G(\bar x).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a continuously differentiable smoothing residual \(F_\mu:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R^m\), define \(\Psi_\mu(x)=	frac12\|F_\mu(x)\|^2\). Then \(
abla\Psi_\mu(x)=
abla F_\mu(x)^{\mathsf T}F_\mu(x)\). Any direction \(d\) satisfying \(
abla\Psi_\mu(x)^{\mathsf T}d<0\) is a descent direction and can be globalized by accepting a step that sufficiently decreases \(\Psi_\mu\). Moreover, \(\Psi_\mu(x)=0\) if and only if \(F_\mu(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The squared norm of the smoothed residual is a differentiable merit function; descent steps reduce it, and its zeros exactly solve the smoothed equation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested smoothing-parameter and backtracking iterations for solving $G(x)=0$.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given $x^0\in\mathbb R^n$, $\varepsilon_0\in\mathcal P$, $\eta,ho>0$, $\gamma\in(0,1/2)$, and $p>2$, initialize $y^{0,k}=x^k$. At an inner iterate, stop if $G(y^{j,k})=0$; otherwise solve $G_{\varepsilon_k}(y^{j,k})+JG_{\varepsilon_k}(y^{j,k})d=0$. If this system is unsolvable or $
abla	heta_{\varepsilon_k}(y^{j,k})^Td\le-ho\|d\|^p$ is not satisfied, replace $d$ by $-
abla	heta_{\varepsilon_k}(y^{j,k})$. Choose the smallest $i_j\ge0$ for which $2^{-i_j}d$ satisfies either the Armijo inequality for $	heta_{\varepsilon_k}$ or $\|G(y^{j,k}+2^{-i_j}d)\|\le	frac12\|G(x^k)\|$, and set $y^{j+1,k}=y^{j,k}+2^{-i_j}d$. If $\|
abla	heta_{\varepsilon_k}(y^{j+1,k})\|\le\eta\|\varepsilon_k\|$ or $\|G(y^{j+1,k})\|\le	frac12\|G(x^k)\|$, set $x^{k+1}=y^{j+1,k}$ and choose $\varepsilon_{k+1}\in\mathcal P$ satisfying $0<\|\varepsilon_{k+1}\|\le\min\{	frac12\|\varepsilon_k\|,	heta(x^{k+1})\}$; otherwise continue the inner iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The algorithm uses a smoothed Newton direction, falls back to steepest descent if the Newton system or descent test fails, backtracks until either Armijo decrease or sufficient residual reduction occurs, and reduces the smoothing parameter after sufficient gradient or residual progress.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Each completed outer iteration sets }x^{k+1}=y^{j+1,k}\text{ and selects }0<\|\varepsilon_{k+1}\|\le\min\{\tfrac12\|\varepsilon_k\|,\theta(x^{k+1})\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \((x_k,\mu_k,\Delta_k)\), compute a step \(d_k\) approximately minimizing \[m_k(d)=\tfrac12\|\Phi_{\mu_k}(x_k)+J_kd\|^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad\|d\|\leq\Delta_k.\] Define \[\rho_k=\frac{\Psi_{\mu_k}(x_k)-\Psi_{\mu_k}(x_k+d_k)}{m_k(0)-m_k(d_k)}.\] Accept \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\) when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\), and otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\), where \(0<\eta_1<1\). Shrink \(\Delta_k\) after poor agreement and permit enlargement when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_2>\eta_1\) and the trust-region boundary is active. Reduce \(\mu_k\) only after the prescribed residual or model-accuracy test; stop when the original complementarity residual meets the requested tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately minimize the smoothed residual model inside a trust region, accept steps by actual-to-predicted reduction, update the radius, and reduce smoothing only after an accuracy test.
